fracas-problems.comment: A synthetic problem set in the released FraCaS shape. Every shape the release uses appears here once: a multi-premise problem, a problem whose question and hypothesis are absent, a qualified answer, a subsubsection, and a pattern gloss.
Q As are Bs == Q As are As who are Bs

problem.p: An Italian became the world's greatest tenor.
problem.q: Was there an Italian who became the world's greatest tenor?
problem.h: There was an Italian who became the world's greatest tenor.

problem.p: Some delegates at the café finished the survey.
Every delegate who finished the survey was on time.
problem.q: Did every delegate finish the survey?
problem.why: Existential quantification over the first argument is not universal.

problem.p: No delegate finished the survey on time.
problem.q: Did Smith finish the survey on time?
problem.h: Smith finished the survey on time.
problem.note: Three premises, so the sequence is three long.

problem.p: Smith wrote to a representative every week.
problem.q: Did Smith write to a representative?

problem.p: When they opened the M25, traffic increased.
problem.note: Original is degenerate problem; no question or answer given.
